question: Should OpenClaw adopt first-declared exact-path ownership, with narrowly defined monotonic exceptions for tools.allow and tools.deny, as the permanent layered-configuration authority contract?
rationale: Tests and lifecycle proof can validate the proposed implementation, but they cannot determine whether this precedence and policy model is the long-term security and compatibility contract maintainers want to support.

options.title: Approve the constrained V1
options.body: Accept the startup-only, opt-in contract after confirming the linked implementation exactly matches the RFC and preserves ordinary configuration behavior.

options.title: Revise the authority model
options.body: Keep the RFC draft open while configuration and security owners change precedence, tightening rules, or mutability boundaries before establishing a public contract.

options.title: Decline core layering
options.body: Close the proposal if OpenClaw should continue receiving only one host-composed effective configuration rather than owning multi-source authority semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve the constrained V1
recommendation.body: Accept the startup-only, opt-in contract after confirming the linked implementation exactly matches the RFC and preserves ordinary configuration behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The available routing and configuration-security history make steipete the strongest candidate to resolve the permanent core contract, with ificator providing configuration-area review.
